quote_text:
Thoughts on that performance Philippe? The football that I want to see and what  
we’ve spoken about the last weeks and months—it’s  about timing, the right runs, the right passes,  
and getting those connections on the pitch. To  gel together with a lot of new players—if you  
see how many new players were on the pitch  today—it's good for the players to get the  
reward for what they've been doing in training and  the games. I don’t think in the last two league  
games they were rewarded in that way because we  also had good chances, but today we finished them  
off—not all of them because it could have been  more. But like this, you see the potential and  
the way this team can play, opening up teams  who want to play a low block and man-marking  
all over the pitch. I think they gave a good  example of how we can be lethal in that way.
You called for more goals at the weekend, and you  got them tonight. How pleased are you with that? 
Yes, that's what I want and what we’ve  spoken about. We want to entertain our fans,  
but it’s not only about the goals; it’s also the  clean sheet. That’s also an important one for me  
today. It was not only about creating chances and  scoring the goals but also not giving anything  
away—not giving belief to the opponent. That’s  also a crucial part that needs to stay in the  
team. I’m for sure happy for the players today  that they got the reward for all the hard work  
they’ve been doing over the last couple of months  in a good team spirit. People from the outside  
can now start to see the potential that can  be in this team, the more they play together.
Is it important to maintain this  level now? Against Ross County,  
you did something similar but fell back after. I think it was a different kind of game against  
Ross County. This was a better level. The other  thing is we have a lot of games coming up in the  
next weeks, so it’s important for the whole squad  to understand what we need at this stage of the  
season. Before, we didn’t have the depth in the  squad with the amount of games. It’s important  
to keep players fit and have players back.  Danilo played a brilliant game today, but he  
was unavailable for almost the last 12 months.  That’s a major thing. Hamza is just coming out  
of a different league, and he’s adapting really  well. There are many examples like that. The way  
Yanis is playing now—it’s important to remember  that many players are only two, three, or four  
months here. It’s normal it wasn’t top yet, but  I want to see more games like this. That’s what  
I’m going to push for. We’re going  to keep improving in every detail.
The front four seemed very fluid tonight.  Egwim and Matondo seemed to work well together. 
Yes, because it’s crucial to have a lot  of movement to come free. It’s difficult  
to play against that kind of system and  create spaces, especially with only one  
training session before the game. But the  players are starting to understand things  
more. We show a lot of video—it’s almost  every day these last months. They’re all  
in the story to make it better in every  detail, whether it’s about runs, crosses,  
finishing, or defensive work. They’re all  really focused. We need to keep it that way  
because then it can only grow and get  better if they stay humble and keep  
working hard like they’ve been doing. I’m really  happy they got the reward now for all their work.
The team selection tonight seemed to set the  tone—it was a very attacking side. Are you feeling  
more comfortable now with your attacking options? Yes, but how many times this year have I had two  
strikers available in the squad? That’s the  reality. It’s major to keep everyone fit. You  
say the right choices, but I’m sure if we hadn’t  won 6-0, maybe you’d have said, “Why is Connor  
Barron not starting today?” That’s how it goes.  All these players are pushing and working hard,  
and we need to keep it that way. They’ll all  have their moments to shine, and they’ll all have  
moments to sit on the bench and be ready for the  next game. This season is such an ultra-marathon  
that we need smart rotation in the squad. That’s  what we’ll do in the coming weeks and months.
Would you consider adding to the front line in  the January window to give you more options? 
We’re going to have big discussions about what we  need in January and, of course, what the budget  
will be. Everything depends on the budget.  We felt that in the summer transfer window,  
too. We wanted more things than we could do—that  was the reality. My job is to get the best out  
of the squad available, push to make it better,  and see how these talks go in the next weeks.
You’ve spoken about showing patience with Hamza.  How excited are you about what he can offer? 
I spoke with a lot of people in Morocco before  bringing him in. Some people who knew him said  
he’s a rough diamond—they didn’t know if  he’d be ready from the start or maybe in  
a year. But we saw the potential, and we  went for it because that’s what the club  
needs to do now. We’ve come out of a period  where the club didn’t have assets to sell,  
making transfers difficult. It’s about hunger  and desire. If he keeps this hunger and desire,  
who knows how far he can go? But  he’s doing really good things.
